currentContext.business: HLV Limited is engaged in the hotel business and, for regulatory purposes, is classified as providing 'infrastructure facilities' under Schedule VI to the Companies Act. Its operations consist of a single luxury hotel, The Leela Mumbai (Sahar, Mumbai), serving premium corporate travellers, retail guests, airline crew, social celebrations and international visitors, together with its restaurant and banqueting offerings. The Company states there has been no fundamental change in the nature of its business during the year ended March 31, 2026, and that it is a service industry without significant manufacturing operations.

currentContext.expansion: The routed text discloses NO hotel capacity addition, new-property or expansion project by the Company itself — HLV Limited remains a single-hotel operator (The Leela Mumbai) and states there has been no fundamental change in the nature of its business during FY 2025-26. The only asset-side additions disclosed are energy assets and efficiency retrofits described under Conservation of Energy: the Company has 3 windmills with a capacity of 4.5 MW power in the State of Maharashtra which continue to produce renewable energy for use in its own hotel, and it has 'installed and commission 230 KW Solar panels on the building rooftop' for renewable solar generation. Other in-hotel investments described are extensive LED and energy-efficient electrical equipment, high-efficiency HVAC systems used/retrofitted extensively, computerized power monitoring, tuning of main chiller plants and steam boilers, a condensate recovery unit for hot water, energy-saving devices in rooms during non-occupancy, an in-house recycled drinking water glass bottling plant serving all guest rooms and restaurants, STP-treated water for cooling tower/garden, and rainwater harvesting. On the property footprint, the Company's hotel land of 18,000 sq. meters and adjacent land of 11,000 sq. meters are held on lease from the Airports Authority of India; the Company has accepted AAI's offer letter dated December 01, 2023 for renewal of the 18,000 sq. meter lease and has requested renewal for a further period of 30 years, with FSI utilisation, land amalgamation and damages referred to arbitration (this land/lease context comes from the profile bundle's Directors' Report text). Technology absorption disclosure is stated to be not applicable as the hotel is a service industry and the Company does not have any significant manufacturing operations.

risks.note: Management states the Company 'continues to face concentration risk arising from heavy dependence on one hotel in Mumbai and exposure to the upper luxury segment' — the entire business is The Leela Mumbai, so any local demand, supply or asset-specific shock is unmitigated by diversification. (Back-filled from the MD&A text delivered in the strategy_outlook bundle; the risks_esg bundle received Directors' Report governance sections instead.)

risks.risk: Airline-crew demand migration to the Navi Mumbai airport ecosystem
risks.note: The Crew segment remained an important contributor, benefiting from Mumbai's position as one of India's busiest aviation hubs, but the ongoing redevelopment and expansion of Terminal 1 at Mumbai Airport together with the commencement of operations at Navi Mumbai International Airport is expected to gradually alter airline operating patterns and crew accommodation requirements, with a portion of crew demand potentially migrating to hotels in the Navi Mumbai micro-market. This is a structural, dated demand risk to a named revenue segment. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A text.)

risks.risk: Land tenure and lease-rental dispute with Airports Authority of India
risks.note: Ongoing disputes over what the Company calls the exorbitant demand of lease rental and royalty in the form of Minimum Guaranteed Amount on the hotel land of 18,000 sq. meters and adjacent land of 11,000 sq. meters, including AAI eviction proceedings. Per the Bombay High Court judgment of June 09, 2025 the lease-rental dispute continues before the AAI Eviction Officer while FSI utilisation, land amalgamation and damages go to arbitration before retired Justice Mr. S.V. Gangapurwala. Renewal of the 18,000 sq. meter lease (the Company has accepted AAI's offer letter dated December 01, 2023 and sought a further 30 years) is still awaited — the site the sole hotel stands on is therefore not on secure long-term tenure. (Back-filled from the Directors' Report text delivered in the profile bundle.)

risks.risk: Unresolved shareholder litigation over the Brookfield transaction
risks.note: ITC Limited and Russell Credit Limited (holding then 8.72%, at present 8.10%) have a Section 241/242/244 oppression-and-mismanagement petition pending, with the Company and promoters Mr. Vivek Nair and Mr. Dinesh Nair appealing the NCLT Mumbai waiver order of January 24, 2024 before the NCLAT, Delhi; ITC's further appeal against the SEBI order (which favoured the Company on July 23, 2019) and the SAT dismissal of September 26, 2019 is pending before the Supreme Court of India. A minority-shareholder overhang on the Company's largest corporate action. (Back-filled from the Directors' Report text delivered in the profile bundle.)

The hotel business continues to be dependent on domestic and global economic conditions, airline connectivity, consumer confidence and the overall geopolitical environment; ongoing geopolitical tensions in conflict-affected regions, trade disruptions, energy-price and crude-oil volatility, airfare volatility, changing travel corridors and inflationary pressure on discretionary spending may influence travel flows, operating costs and discretionary spending. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A text.)

FY 2025-26 occupancy fell to 69% from 73.80% in FY 2024-25, with revenue growth carried by ARR (Rs. 12,469 vs Rs. 11,170) and RevPAR (Rs. 8,602 vs Rs. 8,242); management describes revenue growth as achieved 'despite lower overall room inventory utilisation', and notes that protecting occupancy, average room rates and revenue quality requires sustained sales agility in an environment of geopolitical uncertainty, changing travel behaviour and higher guest expectations. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A Business Review.)

The MD&A cites elevated cyber and security concerns in the global operating environment, and the Board-approved Risk Management Policy framework expressly covers financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability, information and cyber security risks, with measures for risk mitigation including systems and processes for internal control of identified risks and a business continuity plan.

risks.risk: Audit observations on the financial statements
risks.note: The Directors' Report states that although there are no audit qualifications or adverse remarks, there ARE audit observations on the financial statements, with the explanation given in Notes 37.1 and 37.3 — a standing accounting/disclosure watch-item. The routed text does not reproduce the substance of those notes.
